collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — NATURE, ECOLOGY AND ANIMALS (NAT-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Isola's animals, plants, tides and weather: tide pools and nesting beaches, washed-up rubbish, shrinking clam beds, strange visitors, creatures doing what creatures do, and choices about the island where nobody gets a perfect answer.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

collection.description: A villager has heard bat droppings are the best garden food and stands at the bat cave with a scoop: go in at night, or wait.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: There's a cave on the hillside where hundreds of bats sleep through the day. The floor is thick with their droppings, and (subject) has heard, from somebody who heard it from somebody, that bat droppings make the best garden food there is. (subject.He/she) is holding a basket and a scoop and looking at the cave entrance. (friend) is holding (friend.his/her) nose.

text_only.reason: food in the story (a meal, a catch, fruit); the village's stores do not change -- the draft's notes: everything but the marked effects is story only

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (friend) points out that the bats have babies this time of year, and a scoop at the door might frighten them off for good. (subject) sighs and agrees to wait until the young are grown. That evening they sit outside and watch the bats pour out of the cave in a great dark ribbon against the sky. It goes on for ages. Neither of them says anything about droppings for quite a while.

o1__fx.name: Outcome A
o1__fx.text: They wait until dark, when the bats have flown out to feed, and creep in with a torch. It is the smelliest hour of (friend)'s life. But the gardens that get the bat droppings grow like nobody has ever seen. (subject) is very proud. (friend) refuses to talk about the cave, ever, but does start asking for the leftover droppings for (friend.his/her) own beans.
